blocks.text: Human-made sources are either mobile (cars, trucks, aeroplanes, marine engines) or point sources (factories, electric power plants and so on). The combustion of fossil fuels (coal, fuel oils and natural gas) in vehicle engines, factories and power plants produces carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons such as methane. The burning of wood as a domestic fuel and of coal in brick kilns are also sources of air pollutants.

blocks.prompt: Mention the man-made sources of air pollution (Quick Check 14.2a).
blocks.explanation: Mobile sources, the engines of cars, trucks, aircraft and ships, and point sources, factories and electric power plants, all burning fossil fuels and releasing CO2, CO and hydrocarbons; also wood burnt as domestic fuel and coal burnt in brick kilns.

items: Human-made: mobile (vehicles, aircraft, ships) and point (factories, power plants) sources burning fossil fuels, giving CO2, CO, hydrocarbons; wood fuel; coal in brick kilns.
